title: Safe HTML from data
description:
A page will set `list.innerHTML = renderItems(items)`. Write the functions that build that HTML safely: ```javascript function escapeHtml(text) { } // & < > " ' as & < > " ' function renderItems(items) { } // the HTML for a shopping list function highlight(text, query) { } // escaped text with each match of query wrapped in ``` `renderItems([{ name: "Milk", qty: 2, done: false }, { name: "Eggs & ham", qty: 1, done: true }])` gives (as one line, with no spaces between tags): ```html
  • Milk ×2
  • Eggs & ham
``` - The quantity span is only there when `qty` is more than 1. - Done items get `class="done"` after the `data-index`. - An empty list gives `

Nothing to buy.

`. `highlight("Tea tea", "tea")` gives `Tea <b> tea`: matching ignores case, the original letters are kept, and everything is escaped. An empty query gives just the escaped text.
hints: Escape `&` first; otherwise the `&` in `<` would be escaped again.
For `highlight`, search in the lower-case text with `indexOf(q, from)`, but slice the pieces out of the original text so the letters keep their case. Escape each piece separately.
